Retries need limits because every retry consumes time, CPU, memory, connections, and downstream capacity. If failures persist, unlimited retries turn a local error into a feedback loop: clients hammer an overloaded service, amplify traffic, exhaust pools, and deepen the outage. They also add latency and cost, delay failure detection, and can starve healthy requests. Without bounds, retries can create retry storms or thundering herds when many clients retry simultaneously. Limits—max attempts, backoff with jitter, deadlines, and budgets—cap amplification and give systems time to recover. Bounded retries preserve the benefit (transient faults) while preventing permanent faults from becoming permanent damage. Need count ~100. Good. final.

Retries need limits because every retry consumes time, CPU, memory, connections, and downstream capacity. If failures persist, unlimited retries turn a local error into a feedback loop: clients hammer an overloaded service, amplify traffic, exhaust pools, and deepen the outage. They also add latency and cost, delay failure detection, and can starve healthy requests. Without bounds, retries can create retry storms or thundering herds when many clients retry simultaneously. Limits—max attempts, backoff with jitter, deadlines, and budgets—cap amplification and give systems time to recover. Bounded retries preserve the benefit for transient faults while preventing permanent faults from becoming permanent damage.
